method: Both reviewers read every German string of the current file. That covered title and title.canDo, spec.situation and the new spec.deviation (five points), the Folge (10 lines and the gist item), the three inputs (3 × 10 lines) and the LS3 form, the six H1 texts (38 lines), the strategy card, the 8 redemittel, the Sp1 task (instructions, situation, 5 cards, persona, openingLine, 8 hintWords, 9 modelTurns), the S1 task (title, 46-word situation, taskDe, 5 labels, 4 checklist lines, model), the 3 check lines, story.beat and the cliffhanger, the new fact f01, every endLine, modelSentence, aussprache line, promptDe, option and explanation.de, the u02 cards of a1.1/lexicon.json (36 entries) and the three rule cards the unit shows (rc.negation-nicht, rc.ja-nein-frage, rc.praesens-2). We solved all 93 authored items blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line (start gist 1; per LS 5 input + 4 structured + 11 pool + 5 reserve; 6 H1; 8 Check; 3 proof) and the 5 S1 fields. For sentence_building and error_correction we permuted the constituents and checked each V2 or V1 order against accepted[] and the prompt frame. We ran 60 candidate answers through the real grader src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js, the S1 fields exactly as src/components/course-v2/WritingTaskView.jsx FormTask builds them (type form_fill via grade.js gradeAnswer); the results are quoted in F01, F02 and previousFindings. We measured unknown tokens with the validator's own knownForms + licensedForms at a1.1-u02 on the surfaces the LEX-01 walk does not cover (Folge title, story.beat, aussprache focus and readAloud, modelSentences, redemittel, openingLine, hintWords, modelTurns, S1 labels and model, the LS3 form), and looked up every candidate look-ahead in the eight lexicons, names.json, core-lexicon.mjs and grammar-spine.json (g.welch-dies a1.2-u06; g.muessen-duerfen-man chunkFrom a1.1-u08; g.akk-personalpronomen chunkFrom a1.2-u06; g.praep-dativ chunkFrom a1.1-u05; g.trennbare-verben a1.1-u07). We recounted with the validator's wordCount: H1 44/51/35/42/40/47, S1 situation 46, Folge 99, cliffhanger 17. We checked the exam blocks against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json (h1: 6 × abc, 3 options, 2 plays, textWords [32–53], pictorial → textVariantDe scaffold in a1.1; sp1: monologue, prep 0, rubric sd1-sp1 with vorstellen/buchstabieren/nummer, keyword sheet „not all needed“; s1: 5 fields, situation [36–48]) and against registries/rubrics/speaking/sd1-sp1.json. Every task is original in the SD1 format; no official Modellsatz wording was found. We read the can-dos in registries/cando/a1.json, the cast in casts/series.json and casts/a1.json (ages, languages, jobs, voices), and the story against u01, u03 (Folge picks up the cliffhanger; „Alter: 28“), u05 (Berliner Straße 21 = the WG; Arjun 0176 52 83 91 40), u08 and u12 (Priya's number) and u09 (LS1 long/short vowels), which the deviation cites. We read netlify/functions/speaking-turn.mjs for the TTS call behind the Sp1 „schnell“. We tried to re-read fact f01 at deutschepost.de (see notes). Exemplar: u04 and its trail r1–r5, plus u01 r1 and r2; every earlier finding class was checked for recurrence (notes). No 360 px walkthrough was run; that is the walkthrough reviewer's remit.

verdict: Not exit-ready: 0 BLOCKER, 2 MAJOR, 8 MINOR. The unit is clearly better than in r1. 16 of the 21 r1 findings are fixed or fixed within what the SCHEMA allows, and the three r1 rails the rule-smith wrote (the correction-naming rail, the LEX-01 surface walk, det.genitiv-s-name) pass. Every one of the 93 keys and 5 form fields is right. Every H1 option is now heard, and H1 is exact to sd1.json (44/51/35/42/40/47 words, keys 2/2/2). Sp1 asks for all three scored parts and lets the learner invent a number, and S1 has five fields from a 46-word situation. The scene logic of r1 is repaired: Emre calls again, the cliffhanger is an e-mail that u03 picks up word for word, and Lucia lives in Dresden. The deviation is logged and true, and the address fact is verified. Two MAJORs stop exit, and both are correct answers that the real grader rejects. (1) ls1-r04 rejects „04109 ist die Postleitzahl nicht.“ (wrong, tagged v2-inv), although its sister item ls1-p10 in the same Lernschritt accepts exactly that topicalised order. The r1 rule's second half (a correction item accepts the orders its LS accepts) was never written, so ITM-01 passes it (F01). (2) The deterministic S1 form marks „Online-Kurs“ and „Onlinekurs“ wrong in the field „Kurs: in Leipzig oder online?“, and „İzmir, Türkei“ wrong in the field Wohnort. A Goethe marker gives these the point. The cause is a grading method that lists every variant by hand (F02). Eight minors follow. Three are unit-side: look-aheads on German-only item surfaces that no rail reads (F03, two of them from our own r1 wording), isolated phrasing (F04), and one structured-input item that the towns decide rather than the ending (F06). Five are owner-held: proof evidence (F05), the lexicon and names registry (F07), the unchanged rule card (F08), u12's phone number and voice casting (F09), and detector noise (F10). Unit edits needed: one accepted form (F01), four form variants (F02), eleven short string edits (F03), seven (F04) and one item (F06). With the two rails (F01, F02) green, the unit carries 5 owner-held minors and exits.

findings.problem: German-only item surfaces carry grammar that the spine places later, and no rail reads them. GRM-04's instruction scope covers instructionsDe, situationDe, strategy cards and title.canDo, but not promptDe, options, explanation.de or title.de. So det.welch-dies, det.man and det.akkusativ-pronomen-ihn exist but never see these strings. (1) welch- is g.welch-dies (a1.2-u06, no chunkFrom). It stands on an H1 stem without an English twin and on ls2-s02. u01 r2 records that u01 avoids „Welche Sprachen …?“ for this very reason, so the two units now disagree.
